business_problem: I-MED Radiology needed to keep radiology reporting fast and accurate even as the pool of medical typists shrank, but it could not compromise the quality and trust radiologists rely on when signing clinical reports.
solution_summary: I-MED Radiology partnered with Bain to design, build, and deploy an AI-enabled typist that fits directly into the existing reporting workflow. The generative AI system ingests radiologists' dictated findings, drafts the first version of the report, and returns that output inside the same process typists and radiologists already use. Rather than remove human oversight, the solution keeps a typist in the loop so quality, formatting, and clinical trust are preserved while the AI handles much of the transcription burden. Early pilots showed that the AI output was often strong enough to stand alone, but the hybrid operating model let I-MED improve turnaround times and productivity without forcing clinicians to change how they work. The story does not identify a named storage tier or model platform, but it clearly describes a production drafting layer embedded in live radiology operations.

solution_components.name: AI-enabled typist
solution_components.role: Creates draft radiology reports from dictated findings while keeping human typists in the review loop.

data_flow: Radiologists dictate findings, the AI-enabled typist turns that speech into draft reports, and human typists and radiologists review the output within the existing reporting workflow before final sign-off.
business_outcome: The AI-enabled typist improved report turnaround times, multiplied typist productivity, and helped I-MED manage reporting volumes more flexibly without breaking radiologists' preferred formats or review practices.
metrics: 35% improvement in typed report turnaround times
architecture_clues: The solution was designed to slot into the existing workflow rather than replace it.
A typist remains in the loop to preserve quality and accuracy.
The system improves through continuous updates and optimizations.
